title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 19A (Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence)

content.overview: Section 19A provides that when consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. Any such contract may be set aside either absolutely or, if the party who was entitled to avoid it has received any benefit thereunder, upon such terms and conditions as to the Court may seem just.
content.glance: Undue influence → voidable; court may set aside absolutely or on just terms if benefit received.
content.study: Consent caused by undue influence (s. 16) makes the agreement voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. The court may set the contract aside absolutely, or if the avoiding party received benefit, on such terms as seem just. Current-law framing: establish undue influence under s. 16; apply voidability; address restitution terms if benefit was received.

sections.heading: Voidable at option
sections.body: Consent caused by undue influence — agreement voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.

sections.heading: Set aside on terms
sections.body: May be set aside absolutely or, if benefit received, upon such terms as the Court may seem just.

provisions.title: Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence

examples.title: Unconscionable bond
examples.body: A money-lender by undue influence obtains a bond for an excessive sum. The court may set the bond aside on terms requiring repayment of the advance with just interest.

hypotheticals.question: Must the court always set aside the whole contract for free?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. If the avoiding party received benefit, the court may impose just terms under s. 19A.

distinctions.title: Scope of s-19a
distinctions.body: Applies only within the elements and consequences stated in the statutory text.

misconceptions.trap: Undue influence is governed only by s. 19.
misconceptions.correction: Undue influence has its own voidability and terms provision in s. 19A.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 19A problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Establish undue influence (s. 16). II. Apply voidability. III. Address absolute set-aside or terms if benefit received. IV. Conclude.

examTips: State voidability and the power to impose terms.
